- When sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00), model tends to overestimate early in the forecast horizon; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- After a recent spike in price, model often overshoots in the immediate next 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecasted values following a price peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a peak), model tends to hold or overestimate the peak; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in the 10–15 day window post-peak.
- When sentiment history includes positive sentiment (e.g., >0.20), model often overreacts with upward bias; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 10–20 day horizons if sentiment is positive.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome across multiple days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to all forecasted values for the next 7–14 days, especially if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show a downward trend in true outcome, model often fails to capture it; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
